findings.summary: The site ignores the user’s dark-theme preference
findings.evidence: The light and dark screenshots are byte-identical (49,292 bytes), and the preference probe reports computed color-scheme: normal.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens for every surface, including the consent UI.

findings.summary: Text and essential links fail contrast requirements
findings.evidence: axe found 131 color-contrast failures, including 2.93:1 text on #df6d1e, plus four links distinguished only by low-contrast colour.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace low-contrast colour pairs and give inline links a non-colour affordance such as an underline.

findings.summary: Primary result state changes abruptly
findings.evidence: The app injects result HTML into an open shadow root; the probe found no View Transition support or usage and no running transition for the download state change.
findings.suggestedFix: Wrap the result-state update in document.startViewTransition() with a no-motion fallback.

findings.summary: A consent interstitial blocks the entire primary task on first load
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the content dimmed behind a full-screen consent dialog before the downloader can be used.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, content-first consent surface and keep a clearly labelled reject option at the same level as accept.

findings.summary: The consent modal is custom div-based UI rather than a native dialog
findings.evidence: DOM probes found zero dialog, popover, and details elements while the custom .fc-consent-root implements a blocking modal.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a native dialog with correct modal focus management and platform dismissal semantics.

findings.summary: Reusable UI has no component-level responsiveness
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found zero container rules across the long multi-card page; adaptation is viewport-only.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reused cards and downloader panels containment and size-aware @container rules where their layout changes.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated on primary controls
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus on the shadow-DOM URL input and the skip link produced outline-style none; the primary input has no alternative visible focus indicator.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible ring to every link, button, and shadow-root input without removing native outlines.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is very slow and layout stability misses the good range
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 8.6 s and CLS 0.144; the layout primitive independently measured CLS 0.155.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the consent UI from the critical rendering path, reserve its layout, and prioritise the true primary content.

findings.summary: Late consent content causes measurable layout shift
findings.evidence: The layout observer recorded shifts of 0.144 at 2.33 s and 0.010 at 4.61 s, totalling CLS 0.155.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve stable space or render the consent state atomically before first paint; set dimensions for all images.

findings.summary: Blocking scripts and dependency work delay useful content
findings.evidence: HAR confirms parser-inserted jQuery and jquery-migrate without async/defer, while Lighthouse reports an 8.6 s LCP and a 2.48 s LCP element render delay.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove jquery-migrate where possible, defer non-critical scripts, and keep ad/consent dependencies out of the critical chain.

findings.summary: The page ships substantial unused ad and theme code
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimates 262 KiB unused JavaScript and 42 KiB unused CSS; 92.9% of the Flatsome stylesheet was unused.
findings.suggestedFix: Conditionally load ad/consent code after a lawful choice and generate route-level critical CSS instead of the full theme bundle.

findings.summary: Some controls and images lack accessible names
findings.evidence: axe found an unnamed focusable image link; the images primitive found 8 images without alt text, and the downloader text input has no label or aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Label the URL field, name every focusable link, and provide meaningful or empty alt text according to image purpose.

findings.summary: Foreground/background contrast is insufficient across the page
findings.evidence: axe reports 131 serious colour-contrast nodes and four links that rely on colour without a 3:1 difference from body text.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt tested accessible colour tokens and underline links in prose.

findings.summary: Landmarks, heading order, and focus treatment are not robust
findings.evidence: axe found duplicate/nested main landmarks, invalid heading order, and non-unique landmarks; focus probes found no visible outline.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep one top-level main, repair heading order, uniquely label repeated landmarks, and add :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: Image asset hygiene is inconsistent
findings.evidence: The images primitive found 1 image without dimensions, 3 oversized images, 3 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, and 8 missing alt values.
findings.suggestedFix: Set intrinsic dimensions, use responsive srcset/sizes, lazy-load below-fold images, and repair alt text.

findings.summary: Deprecated APIs execute during page load
findings.evidence: Lighthouse recorded three deprecated API warnings from the Cloudflare challenge script, including deprecated Shared Storage and persistent storage usage.
findings.suggestedFix: Update or configure the challenge integration so it does not execute deprecated browser APIs.

findings.summary: Security headers and cookie attributes are weak
findings.evidence: HTTPS is used, but CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame protection, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy are absent; 3 analytics/consent cookies are not Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a staged CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure with appropriate SameSite.

findings.summary: Advertising and analytics dominate the network footprint
findings.evidence: The tracker probe found 11 third-party origins and three known trackers; HAR shows 642,413 third-party bytes, 74% of all transferred bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Minimise vendors, delay non-essential analytics/ads until consent, and prefer batched first-party measurement.

findings.summary: Browser-enforced defensive policies are absent
findings.evidence: The headers primitive found no HSTS, clickjacking protection, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy, CSP, or nosniff protection.
findings.suggestedFix: Add HSTS, CSP frame-ancestors, nosniff, strict-origin-when-cross-origin, and a least-privilege Permissions-Policy.

findings.summary: The core downloader disappears without JavaScript
findings.evidence: Raw HTML exposes 94% of content copy, but the downloader is created by attachShadow() and event listeners in inline JavaScript; the no-JS crawler cannot operate the core tool.
findings.suggestedFix: Render a labelled URL form in HTML that posts to the existing endpoint, then enhance it with shadow DOM and AJAX.

findings.summary: Missing URLs silently redirect to the homepage
findings.evidence: A request for /web-uplift-missing-404 returned a 301 and rendered the homepage title and downloader instead of a 404 with recovery guidance.
findings.suggestedFix: Return a real 404 status and a focused not-found page with search/home recovery links.

findings.summary: Consent is easier to accept than refuse
findings.evidence: The first-layer dialog offers Consent and Manage options but no Reject all; rejection requires another layer while accepting is one click.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide equally prominent Accept all and Reject all actions on the first layer and minimise default purposes/vendors.

findings.summary: Downloader errors are visual-only and use an opaque error code
findings.evidence: Invalid input yields “Paste correct link and try again 0x03” by replacing innerHTML, with no aria-live/status semantics exposed by the shadow host.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate the URL after interaction, associate clear guidance with the input, and announce errors through role=status or aria-live.

findings.summary: The primary URL field does not expose URL input semantics
findings.evidence: The field is type=text with no label, autocomplete token, inputmode, or URL-specific validation despite requiring a TikTok URL.
findings.suggestedFix: Use type=url, a visible label, inputmode=url, spellcheck=false, and descriptive validation.

findings.summary: Most image elements use legacy formats or lack responsive delivery
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports 54 legacy-format images, 3 oversized images, 1 missing srcset, and 3 below-fold images not lazy-loaded.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve content images as AVIF/WebP with srcset/sizes and lazy-load below-fold assets.

findings.summary: Non-core advertising work outweighs the product code
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 629,868 script bytes and Lighthouse estimated 262 KiB unused JS, mostly ad, analytics, and consent scripts.
findings.suggestedFix: Load non-essential scripts only after consent and interaction, and remove redundant analytics and migration code.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts consume most transferred bytes
findings.evidence: Third parties transfer 642,413 of 862,683 bytes; AdSense, Tag Manager, Funding Choices, and fonts are the largest origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Set and enforce a third-party byte/request budget, self-host the one needed font subset, and defer ads.

findings.summary: The downloader has no structured agent-facing capability
findings.evidence: Lighthouse agentic browsing scored 0.26 and found no well-formed agent accessibility tree or llms.txt; the actionable downloader lives inside shadow DOM with no WebMCP tool.
findings.suggestedFix: Expose the downloader as a safe, validated agentic form or WebMCP tool while retaining the standard HTML form.

findings.summary: The initial footprint is large for a simple downloader
findings.evidence: The baseline heap contains 381,113 nodes and 21.84 MB self size, while the rendered consent DOM lists hundreds of vendor controls before interaction.
findings.suggestedFix: Virtualise or defer vendor detail DOM and load only the consent summary initially.
